slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that make you
addicted to discipline

logging your runs

run three times a week and write every run in a notebook. watching your times slowly drop is more addictive than any screen, and it keeps you going week after week.

one song a month

learn one full song on an instrument every month. the moment you finally play it through without a mistake is a rush that makes you want to practise more.

a daily learning streak

learn something new for 5 minutes a day and never break the streak. protecting a small daily streak trains discipline faster than any big ambitious plan.
slides.texte_sophia:
a daily learning streak

i keep a daily learning streak. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, a planet or a myth, and not wanting to break that streak made me disciplined everywhere.

slides.texte_overlay:
growing from seed

grow vegetables from seed on a balcony or in a garden. caring for them every day and waiting patiently teaches your brain that slow effort really pays.

cold morning walks

go for a twenty minute walk every morning before breakfast, even in winter. doing something hard first thing makes the rest of the day feel so much easier.
